O best of Brahmins, know that everything is established by means of that which is established.
This applies to the circumambulation and prostration previously performed upon the temple, from its very foundation up to the pinnacle of its banner. (348)
Having circumambulated the deity and prostrated with the eight limbs, and having taken up the vessel for the *arghya* offering, one should go outside the temple. [The Offering of the Bali] (349)
And one should complete the offering of oblations to the many spirits:
"May the spirits outside the temple, who are devotees of the Blessed One, accept [this]. (350)
Having offered the bali-oblation, the mantra-purification, and [the offerings] for those who are their followers, with a vessel containing water, and having bowed to the deity— || 351 ||
[The Full Oblation for the Pacification of Deficiencies and Excesses:
Thereafter, he should go to the sacrificial hall and perform the full oblation (pūrṇahoma);
then, for the sake of remedying any deficiency or excess, he should offer the full oblation. || 352 ||
[Now, the declaration of the fruit:
O Nārada, from the ground where the temple stands to the end of the flagpole of the pavilion, including all its furnishings down to the subtlest atoms— 353.
For as many times as the number [of recitations] that is produced, for that many [lifetimes] shall the performer abide;
enjoying pleasures in the world of Viṣṇu, he goes at the end to the supreme state. || 354 ||

[The Worship of Those Invited for the Consecration Rite: Then, having worshipped all those previously mentioned in due order according to the rules, with perfumes, water for the guest-offering (arghya), flowers, incense, garlands, and unguents; || 355 ||
O great sage, one should worship with various foods according to one's ability and with sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
[Now, the night vigil:
One should perform a night vigil, a great festival with dance and song. (356)
[The necessity of performing the fire-oblation for four days starting from the consecration]:
One should perform the fire-oblation continuously for four days, according to the specific moments and weekdays, both externally in the sacrificial pits and internally. (357)
Just as there is no cessation of the smoke for four days, so indeed it is there;
[regarding the ritual of bathing and so forth on the fourth day from the consecration]: When the fourth day has arrived, having bathed the Supreme Lord... (358)
Having performed worship according to the previous procedure, one should perform the fire oblation (homa) according to one's capacity;
then, having offered the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) for the entire network of mantras.

[Now, the worship of Viṣvaksena: O twice-born one, according to the procedure previously described, inside the temple— in the northeast corner— Viṣvaksena is to be worshipped while seated upon a movable pedestal, or within a water-filled pitcher.
Having worshipped Viṣvaksena, the guardians of the forms (mūrtipās) should also be worshipped.
[The manner of utilizing the remaining materials: Having completed all the preparations and having offered them to one's own guru... || 361 ||
Or, if the twice-born preceptor himself performs the installation,
he must diligently distribute [the fees] among the image-makers and others in due order.
One should bathe with the *avabhṛtha* rite for the sake of attaining the desired goal of both worldly success (*siddhi*) and liberation (*mukti*).
This has been taught for the practitioner who desires the propitiation of the mantra. (363)
The installation of the mantra-form is that wherein one, being established, attains accomplishment.
[Regarding the specific procedure for the installation of a painting: O Sage, for those situated on plaster, walls, or cloth, the bathing and other rites are performed before a mirror. 364.
One should perform worship with flowers from which the water has been removed, leaving nothing remaining;
O twice-born one, [therein follows] the prohibition against the placement of jewels when installing images that are fixed on walls or situated on cloth-paintings. 365.

The ritual procedure known as the installation of the pedestal, the Brahma-stone, and the jewels would not apply [in other cases]; however, O Nārada, for those made of metal and the like, which have pedestals of a similar origin, that procedure [is applicable]. (366)
One should perform [the rites] for moving images with small bodies;
indeed, it is exactly the same for those made of stone, clay, or wood, and not otherwise.
If there is no core support, one should indeed remember the inner core with the intellect.
[Now follows the procedure for the restoration of what is decayed; therein is the prohibition against worshipping a decayed image:
When a cloth painting or a wall painting has perished, or when an image has been broken through negligence, || 368 ||
O Brahmin, worship is not ordained [for you], nor is worship truly auspicious;
therefore, O high-minded one, having performed worship with a specific fire-oblation (homa), [proceed]. (369)

One should initiate within the heart the entire sequence of giving and worship directed toward the ascetics who know the reality of the Blessed One, according to the very order of their incarnations. (370)
O Sage, having placed the collection of supports according to the previously stated procedure,
one should cast it into a body of water with the mantra of Viṣvaksena, as if performing the ritual of placement and worship for a broken image made of other mineral substances. (371)
For in a deep body of water, in the absence of the emergence of metallic substances, there is no refinement for the work of a reflected image. (372)
This has been fully described regarding the single-bodied images;
now hear from me concerning those images that are joined together with the Vajrabandha seal, having been specially integrated with one another along with the pīṭha. || 373 ||

[In that regard, there is faultlessness in the partial breaking of the pedestal: However, when a portion of the pedestal is broken, no fault arises. [Regarding slight injury to a limb, there is rejoining: In the case of a minor injury to a limb, it may be repaired.
If there is a slight injury to a limb of the image, one should perform a rubbing with gold.
[On the excessive breaking of the pedestal: its abandonment] When there is a major breakage, one should lift the image from the pedestal and discard it;
having fashioned a new pedestal, one should then re-install it there once more. || 375 ||
[Discarding the image when its deterioration is excessive]: When the image is broken, even if the pedestal remains auspicious, it is prescribed that a new image be made.
[The procedure for when the placement of the seed-syllables is unknown]: In such a case, the rite is performed with the *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*).
For when the deposition of the seed-syllables (bīja) is not understood, the reality of Brahman remains hidden within them.

In this rite, the knower of reality should diligently extract all forms of knowledge and the mantras from their respective places into the *praṇava*; for all mantras reside within the *praṇava*. || 377 ||
Since the relationship between the signified and the signifier belongs to those two alone and to nothing else, O Brahmin, by this method [the merit] of the constructed sanctuary is established. (378)
It remains for a period beyond the reach of sensory objects and does not undergo disappearance again.
(p. 229) [In times of calamity such as the destruction of one's country, it must be protected through focused attention:
"But in the event of the ruin of the country, death, famine, or extreme distress," (379)
If, due to the fear of drought, a location must be inspected,
the image shall not incur impurity because of the predominance of its presence.
Through contact with thieves and the like, or by frequenting that [place],
whichever excellent counselor is devoted and a practitioner who has made a firm resolve— 381.
He shall attain here, without delay, the success desired in his mind.
[The prescription for performing the great festival:
A bright day accompanied by an auspicious constellation and joined with a benign planet. (382)
Relying on ministers who are favorable toward the country, the builder, the king, and others, the king should act; for even a Vaiṣṇava builder is indeed blessed. (383)
With reference to the great omen, he shall hold a grand festival for three years,
according to the very rites prescribed for his own country.
Having abandoned the ritual image situated in the celestial chariot, or alternatively the discus and other symbols,
accompanied by the sounds of dancing and singing, songs, and preceded by the offering of musical instruments.
Accompanied by the *balikarma* (offering of oblations), it should be made to circumambulate for the sake of perfect peace;
this is for the attainment of the fruits of fame and merit for all the villages and other settlements. (386)
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Procedure for Consecration," in the glorious *Jayākhyasaṃhitā* of the *Pāñcarātra*.
Now begins the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Ritual of the Purifier" (Pavitravidhāna).
Nārada: [Question regarding the method of expiation in the event of the omission of ritual performance.]

O Blessed One, for a practitioner established in the observances who is intent on his practice, [if he should fail] through delusion, or due to the collapse of the country, or because he is afflicted by diseases such as fever; || 1 ||
If the performance of a rite is incomplete due to some defect in the ritual action, what should be done with it, O Lord? Or what would happen to that person? Please tell me.
The Blessed Lord: [Regarding the prescription of the Pavitrāropaṇa as an expiation: By means of the performance of ritual action, recitation, and burnt offerings...
And for the practitioner whose ritual actions, recitations, worship, and so forth have been neglected. || 3 ||
"O Brahmin, apart from the offering of the *pavitra*, there can be no other way [to attain liberation].
Nārada: [A question regarding the method for the procedure of offering the *pavitra*]
I wish to hear, in accordance with the truth, about the Pavitrāropaṇa rite of Viṣṇu.
"By means of which I may have fulfilled my purpose, for I am indeed ever intent upon ritual action.
The Blessed Lord said:
[The Prescribed Time and Ritual for the Investiture of the Sacred Thread].
When the Sun is situated in Cancer, or when it is situated in Leo, Virgo, or Libra; || 5 ||
On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, or on the full moon day, wherever one pleases,
[one should perform the rites] according to the prescribed rule for the sake of pacifying any omissions in the performance of recitation and fire-offerings.
Having performed the sacrifice in the section concerning the *pavitraka*, and having done that which was previously mentioned,
one should perform the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsa*) of the materials— such as the threads and so forth— in accordance with the ritual rules on the tenth day.
And one should indeed provide threads for those [images];
know that those threads are produced from silk cloth (or, understand that there is an option regarding the threads being made of silk and so forth).
It may be made of cotton or linen, smooth and firmly woven.
Having first performed its purification through burning and nourishing,
one should then meditate upon it as consisting of the five elements in its all-pervading nature.
[Now, the procedure for preparing the sacred thread (pavitra) with threads:
First, having made it threefold, one should then make it fourfold, since the twice-born thereby produces the equality of all states of being. (10)
Therefore, one should not make that very thread with uneven strands;
with that thread, O best of Brahmins, one should then begin the purifiers (pavitra).
[The number of sacred threads (pavitra) to be offered for each mantra in the maṇḍala]:
O Nārada, for the entire wheel of mantras beginning with the root mantra,
there should be three, three, or else two, two, or one each, provided that such is possible according to the truth.
O Nārada, for each of the secondary rites (*anukalpa*), one should prepare a *pavitraka* thread;
[regarding the rule for the extent, knots, and number of those *pavitra*s:
one should fashion it in the shape of a stream with threads equal to half the length of the *vyāsa*. (13)
The first [section] should be with one hundred and eight [verses], the second with double that, and the third with triple; one should thus arrange it according to Vyāsa.
The first [type of cloth] has thirty-six knots; the second is remembered as being double that;
the third is triple, O Brahmin—[this is the procedure for dyeing and so forth of those possessing pure fragrance].
Indeed, one should [apply] a knot with saffron. || 15 ||
One should dye it with sandalwood and other substances according to its beauty,
using a soft, very white thread that is uniform and knotted.
O Nārada, one should fill the space between the two nostrils so that it takes the shape of a conch shell,
for the purpose of worshipping the mantra-forms within the maṇḍala.
The measurement for the sacred threads (pavitra) has always been declared according to Vyāsa;
[this constitutes the prescription for the different shapes and measurements of the sacred threads according to the specific parts of the image, beginning with the head].
Of an installed image, or one made of precious substances and the like. || 18 ||
And one should place a garland upon the head, with knots and fillings as desired, hanging down from the two shoulders as far as the kneecaps. (19)
From the top of the head down to the feet, this third section is very extensive;
one should indeed construct a beautiful separate pedestal according to its own proper measurement. [This is the rule for the dimensions of the pedestal and the purificatory rite. 20.

[The detailed rule for the *pratisarā* cords: The detailed measurement of the image-*pratisarā*s is also recorded as being indefinite; however, when possible, the length of the cord should be double the previously stated measurement of the thread. (21)
O best of sages, one should then tie three strands together and fill them out;
knots should be placed at equal intervals of three finger-breadths for all of them.
Without enumerating them, these auspicious [vessels] are like citrons;
[this is the rule for the method of fashioning the purification vessels such as the *kumbha*:
specifically, they are placed in front of the two excellent *kumbhas* and indeed before the seat of knowledge (*vidyāpīṭha*). 23.
O Nārada, [one may worship] with the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles, the bell, and the rosary;
and for the *arghya* vessel, one may use a single thread containing [the mantra] according to one's desire.
[The specific varieties of the purification ritual for the six [categories], beginning with the Guru, in their respective order:
O best of sages, one should perform the rite for ascetics who know the pledges of the Guru and others, and for those of purified soul, as well as for householders, using threads in due sequence. (25)
O Brahmin, [he should worship] with twenty-four threads, and likewise with sixteen;
then with twelve, and immediately after that with eight.

Then, knots should be tied according to the number of threads—six, three, and [the remainder]—and one should dye them according to the previous rule; one should not perform the filling of the interior.

[The Ritual Procedure for the Consecration of the Pavitra] (Therein, the method for placing the pavitras): Having established them indeed upon a leaf, in a vessel, or in a cup made of *palāśa* leaves,
one should afterwards cover them with a very white, unwashed cloth.
Having placed that vessel in the midst of the sacrificial materials,
one should bathe according to the previous rule and perform the daily worship of Hari, preceded by the ritual for the special sacrifice. (29)
Then, by means of the sequence known as initiation (dīkṣā),
one should perform the specific sacrifice, having completed everything beginning with the door-sacrifice (dvārayāga) and preceded by the ritual of the water-pot (kalaśa).
O best of sages, having first performed worship accompanied by oblations and the satiation with mantras in this manner, one should carry out the ritual arrangement.
Then, after performing the binding of mudrās and the recitation of mantras, one should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
O Brahmin, this was performed on a day in a previous year that has now passed.
One should remember the withdrawal of the purificatory thread (pavitraka) starting from that very day;
one should worship the entire sacrifice with offerings of water for honor (arghya), flowers, and oblations (bali).
Having sipped water for purification, one should then recollect the entire collection of mantras in their proper sequence,
whether the image was previously consecrated or fashioned by oneself.
Having emerged, one should then bathe [the deity] with devotion according to the previously mentioned procedure;
then, having worshipped [him] especially and having offered the *arghya* once again, (p. 233).
Having recollected the root mantra together with the mudrā for recitation,
one should remember everything done or left undone during the preceding day, as before.
Having performed a circumambulation, he should go once more to the sacrificial hall;
there, having offered oblations to the Mantra-form residing upon the ground, he should perform the ritual of worship at the four locations.
Betel, a tooth-stick, and the five products of the cow, preceded by these,
[should be placed] in front of the God of gods, specifically to the right of the lion-form.
O Nārada, one should offer a lamp, incense, a mirror,
and a golden thread to the Kāpila image in the west, as well as a golden vessel.
Then, having offered a full oblation of sacrificial ghee in the Vārāha and Uttara [fires],
one should likewise offer garlands, medicinal herbs, water, milk, and honey.
Fruits, grains of śāli rice, and tooth-sticks for others, along with betel leaf, and then the *pratisara* cord, O Sage. (41)

Having offered [the oblation] from the vessel, one should perform it in the same manner for the water-pot (kumbha) and the fire; likewise, outside the image, everything up to the end of the *pratisarā* rite should be performed.
[The Invitation: Then, one should invite the desired mantra according to the proper sequence:
"O Lord of Gods, you have been invited; the sacrifice has been performed according to the ritual rule. (43)
"O Blessed One, bring that which fulfills all rites. Having thus addressed the Lord who abides in the various forms of Manu, [he spoke]. 44.

[Encircling the sacrificial seat with thread: Immediately thereafter, one should encircle the sacrificial seat with a white thread that has been wound three times and is provided with a needle, leaving an interval between the turns. || 45 ||
Having covered the sacred objects individually with very firm vessels,
O Brahmin, one should likewise encircle the temple from the outside in the manner previously described.
O Nārada, one should properly offer the *bhūtabali* with the *astra-mantra*. [The procedure for consuming the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and other rites follows.]
Having first drunk the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) and having eaten food placed in the sacrificial oblation (caru), [he should proceed]. || 47 ||

Having thoroughly chewed the tooth-stick or betel leaf as desired, one should sip water (ācamana), perform the ritual placement (nyāsa), and then effect the complete constitution of the body (sakalīkaraṇa). (48)
One should extract the mantra from its place and install it either in the water-pot or within oneself.
[The procedure for the night vigil and the completion of the mandala rite:
One should perform the night vigil and complete the mandala. (49)
Then, at the end of the night, one should bathe and worship Acyuta according to one's means.
[The procedure for the method of offering the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa): therein, the worship of the four locations preceded by the daily ritual.]
Having first performed the daily rites, one should worship the deity residing in the water-pot according to the prescribed sequence.
O twice-born one, thereafter [the deity] is established in the maṇḍala; immediately after that, in the fire;
and preceded by the ritual bath, it is established in the image within the temple.

[First: The Method for Placing the Purifier upon the Vessel] Having entered the sacrificial hall and gone to the vicinity of the vessel, one should worship it, open the protective covering (*prātisarīyaka*), and [proceed]. (52)
Having looked upon and taken hold of it, he should meditate upon all that— whatever ritual action was performed throughout the year— from dawn until the end of night— for that twice-born man.
Having properly recollected that partless state arising from meditation, which is indeed the station of liberation,
one should recollect the partless mantra according to the sequence of pure articulation.
Having joined the mantra with that thread, and likewise the thread with the mantra,
one should unite them with oneself and place [the thread] upon the head of the mantra.
Having undertaken the supreme Sūtra, one should meditate for a year upon that [deity] in his entirety and in his parts— the very nature of both knowledge and action— while performing ritual action.
Having recollected the mantra of both forms worshipped in the jar,
and having performed the mental connection as before, one should offer the sacred thread (pavitraka).
Then, O Brahmin, one should bring forward the third *pratisara*,
and one should recollect the entire and complete external ritual performed throughout the year.
One should worship one's own self, from the foundational level up to the supreme limit,
by means of the entire self through the sequence known as dissolution, enjoyment, and authority.

Having recollected the entire Lord of Mantras, whose form consists of dissolution, enjoyment, and so forth, and having performed the reconnection (*sandhāna*), one should then offer the protective amulet (*pratisara*).
One should perform the threefold worship by means of water for the guest-offering (arghya), flowers, garlands, incense, and unguents, alternating them in sequence. (61)
O best of Brahmins, having thus offered the purifying thread (pavitraka) to the one residing in the water-pot with the root mantra and the soul-attuned Gāyatrī, O son, O Brahmin, [proceed].

[The Offering of the Purifiers to the One Seated in the Maṇḍala] O Nārada, according to this rite, one should first offer three bright purifiers (pavitraka) to the one seated in the maṇḍala at the place of enjoyment.
One should offer three or one [of the requisites] for all the mantras according to one's desire.

Then, having worshipped the omnipresent Lord residing in the fire and subsequently that residing in the image, [the rite of] the installation of the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa) is performed for both the one in the fire and the one in the image. || 64 ||
By means of the procedure prescribed for the *kalaśa*, with three ornaments each, O Brahmin, one should offer them into the fire;
however, one should not perform a *homa* sacrifice with the ornaments. (65) [This is the specific determination regarding the offering to that which resides in the fire.]
Since renunciation has been prescribed as the ultimate goal for one who is adorned, it is not proper to seize it; for to burn it [is improper] without first taking away its blemish.
O Nārada, after the period of the *pavitraka* rite has passed, for the practitioners,
one should subsequently assume the lotus posture (*padmāsana*) and stand facing the deity. (67) [The Procedure for the Recitation of the Great Mantra]
By reciting this great mantra even once, which increases the efficacy of all rites,
one destroys the faults of transgressing the samaya rules merely by remembering it.
[Now, the announcement: Then he should announce to the Lord, who is situated in the three places, in due order:
"Whether intentionally or unintentionally, the regular worship has not been performed. (69)
O Supreme Lord, because of some defect caused by obstacles, my mind suffers from an intense torment that is like fire. (70)
"O Janārdana, since I am afflicted by the fault of my own vow,
O Lord, that which was previously ordained by you out of a desire for the welfare of your devotees— " (71)
This pure and purifying work, which destroys all faults, has been composed by me;
be gracious to me, grant me protection, and indeed abandon your anger born of offense. (72)
Salutations, salutations to you, O Soul of Mantra! Be gracious, O Supreme Lord, to me who am sinking in the ocean of existence and have fallen away from the observance of the pledge. 73.
Protect, protect me, O Lord of the three worlds, destroyer of Keśava’s distress! By your grace, may no fault arise in me regarding that which is known as the *samaya*. (74)
"O Lord, let there be today the perfection of my daily and occasional rites.
Having heard this with respect from him who was afflicted by worldly existence, the King of Mantras [spoke].
It swiftly leads to the state of fullness and destroys the defects pertaining to the time-periods.
[Now, the worship of the Guru:
Having performed this, one should then worship the Guru with devotion as if he were Viṣṇu. (76)
Others who were devoted to the Blessed One were received with gifts according to their means, as well as various drinks and foods, and were likewise restrained. || 77 ||

[The description of the superior fruit of the gifts given to ascetics and others at the conclusion of the Pavitra festival: O Nārada, there are five types beginning with the Vaikhānasa, and four beginning with the Yati; furthermore, there are four classes of people beginning with the Brāhmaṇa, distinguished by the five categories starting with the Āpta. || 78 ||
The five [gifts], beginning with *yogarata* and ending with *śāstrasandhāraṇa*, are proclaimed as being given in incalculable measure to an ascetic who is a Vaiṣṇava. (79)
Know that what is given to one who is solely devoted is indeed multiplied ten millionfold;
whereas what is given to a wearer of the topknot (śikhin) is indeed less than a thousandth part of that.
O Nārada, know that in the rite of the *pratisara* thread, the gift given to a Vaikhānasa is reduced by one-tenth, while that given to a Sātvata is reduced by one-hundredth. (81)
Thus has it been declared regarding the four types of twice-born who are worthy recipients;
now hear concerning the reduction of the gift for those who are unworthy, up to the point of striking [them]. || 82 ||
It is proclaimed that for one who is not an Āpta, the merit is multiplied by a hundred thousand; and the same applies to giving food many times to many Brāhmaṇas. 83.
O best of Brahmins, whether he be a practitioner or a non-practitioner, whoever casts [this away], for him success quickly arises both in this world and in the next. (84)
O tiger among sages, I have thus described to you, by a hundred-thousandth part, this fulfillment of the ritual actions for practitioners.
O Nārada, having given even a hundredth part of that share to the king and others, one then attains her [the fruit] through a gift three times half a lakh (fifteen thousand). (86)
Whatever is given according to the prescribed rite to a Brahmin who wears his sacred thread over the shoulder (añjalīyaka), that [gift] would diminish by a thousandth or a hundredth part. || 87 ||
Henceforth, I shall describe the gift for those undertaking [the rite], ranging from kings down to Śūdras;
it is held that for a Brāhmaṇa who has undertaken [the rite], the gift should be a hundred-thousand-fold.
Know that for those beginning with the Kṣatriyas, it is less by one-tenth of a thousandth part;
however, a gift given to a Brāhmaṇa who is well-established in his duties is ten-thousandfold greater. 89.
Know that for a king it is multiplied a thousandfold, or even designated as a hundredfold; ten times greater than that is for those proficient in yoga and knowledge—listen further to this.

A gift given to a Brahmin who knows the yoga of the Blessed One and is the best among those who know the Vedas yields merit ten million times ten millionfold; it is devoid of even a thousandth part of what is given to others.
For one of the Kṣatriya caste, it is that same [result] reduced by a hundredth part; for one of the Vaiśya birth, it is reduced by a tenth part;
and for a Śūdra who practices yoga devoted to the Lord, it is reduced by a tenth part of that.
For the best of the twice-born who is devoted to recitation, the merit is indeed a hundred thousand-fold;
for kings and others, it is less by a thousandth part, a hundredth part, or a tenth part respectively.
O Nārada, for a Brāhmaṇa ascetic of Viṣṇu, [the merit] is multiplied by ten million;
for Kṣatriyas and others, it is less than that by a thousand and so forth, as previously stated.
But a gift given at a pure time to an excellent twice-born who knows the Nārāyaṇa-āgama is remembered as being a hundred times ten millionfold [in merit]. (95)
One should arrange that for the Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras as previously described;
and for the Brāhmaṇa who, out of devotion, upholds the scriptures of the Vaiṣṇavas. || 96 ||
And it is said that a gift given to them becomes ten billion times more meritorious;
this [gift] prescribed for the Kṣatriyas and others would be a thousandfold and so forth.
[The Worshipfulness of Any Vaiṣṇava] O best of Brahmins, whatever Vaiṣṇava may be present there at that time, he should be worshipped according to one's ability and with devotion. 98.
O great sage, let alone the being who is by nature a Vaiṣṇava;
even any devotee whatsoever who has arrived having assumed the Vaiṣṇava mark is worthy of worship. (99)
"I am indeed a Vaiṣṇava seeking wealth; give it!"—thus he speaks repeatedly.
O Nārada, even if he is unknown, such a person should be honored with effort according to one's ability. (100)

O twice-born one, the consecrated purifiers (pavitra) should be kept exactly as they were in the maṇḍala and other locations until the time of their removal— whether for one night, three nights, or seven nights.
The purifying thread (pavitraka) should be placed within the mandala, as well as that which pertains to the ritual worship.
Alternatively, O Brahmin, having likewise established the ornaments upon the image,
one should wait until the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) of the bright fortnight of Kārtika arrives.
Having removed the flower offerings every single day, once the designated day has arrived, the *pavitraka* should be applied again. 103.

[The Procedure for the Method of Disposing of the Pavitra] Having removed it with devotion and offered it to the Guru or to a Brāhmaṇa who is engaged in the five-fold daily rites (pañcakāla)— in the absence of such a person, O Nārada— 104.
For one who is truly devoted to Viṣṇu and intent upon the six rites,
having performed the special sacrifice ending with the fire-oblation (homa), there should be the worship of the preceptor (ācārya).
The Vaiṣṇavas should be worshipped as before, and then one should give them clothing according to one's ability, O Nārada, or even if such is unavailable.
One must certainly provide either a pair or a single garment for one [deity];
for the others, one should arrange sacred threads together with upper garments.
[The Request in the Presence of Ascetics:
Then, a request should be made to the ascetics of restrained self:
"By the power of your grace, may my fulfillment be attained. (108)
"And may there be no transgression of the samaya for me regarding all the constituent parts of the ritual.
[Then, the response of the ascetics and others:
"So be it," should be said by all in unison with the rhythmic beat (tāla). 109.
O Sage, the fault of improper actions committed throughout the year, even when preceded by a formal agreement,
quickly goes to destruction through the Pavitrārohaṇa rite.

[The Etymology of the Word *Pavitra*] Because it protects that which is possessed of fault from falling, and because it especially purifies the twice-born (*dvija*) and performs complete action, it is called *pavitra*. (111)
And because the practitioner might be devoid of ritual action, I have therefore described this great sacrifice called the *pavitra*, characterized by the previously stated definitions. (112)

[Special observances to be maintained after the performance of the Pavitraka rite: O Brahmin, once the Pavitraka rite has been performed by devotees intent on the practice of mantras, certain special observances must be diligently maintained. (113)
O best of Brahmins, the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika is exceedingly meritorious; furthermore, from that point onward, one should diligently observe the five-day period.
One should perform some act devoted to a vow, preceded by charity and worship, which pacifies all defects and increases all happiness. (115)
Honey, meat, untruth, sexual intercourse accompanied by hunting, anointing with oil, fish, and eating much food frequently; || 116 ||
O best of Brahmins, whether he be a practitioner or a non-practitioner, whoever casts [the obstacle] away, for him success arises thus both in this world and in the next. || 117 ||
Thus, O tiger among sages, I have related this sacred and sin-destroying account for the completion of the rites of those who seek spiritual perfection.
For those devoted to the propitiation of mantras, it is a great bestower of siddhi without delay;
yet for devotees devoid of mantra and tantra within the three worlds, [it remains inaccessible]. (119)
It constantly bestows the fruit of the purificatory rite (pavitra) until its completion.
Nārada said:
Who is that mantra to be recited by those devoted to ritual action, which pertains to the Creator of the Universe? (120)
"At the conclusion of the worship, however, tell it to me as it truly is.
The Blessed One said:
"[The Great Mantra, which was previously mentioned as that which is to be recited at the conclusion of the Pavitraka rite,]"
First there are three *oṃ* syllables, and after that, the first [syllable] alone. || 121 ||
Then there is Pavitra, Ṛtadhāman, and Parā Prakṛti;
at the end of that is Tālalakṣmā, and then Buddhi, marked by Ānanda.
One should give the letter *ra* marked with the vowel sign (*ākāra*), and immediately after that, the letter *ya* alone; O best of the twice-born, it is likewise [called] Śāstā. (123)
"I have taken refuge in you; therefore, protect me, protect me, together with the word-pair.
Then, taking the letter *ma*, adorned with the bliss of the Lord of Space (*vyomeśānanda*). (124)
At the end are the two *sarva-vajras*, followed by *damana* joined with *vikramī*.
*Nṛsiṃha* is at the end, granting success (*siddhida*), adorned with the letter *ya* and the triangle. (125)
Halāyudha (Ha) is situated in the letter A and adorned with the visarga;
then, taking the letter Sa, there follows the one residing in Varuṇa (Va), and after that, Anala (Ra).
The letter *sa* and the letter *ma*, followed by that which is extremely subtle (*su-sūkṣma*),
and the letter *va*— which is joined with *oṃ* and preceded by the gods (*vibudha*)— is endowed with a physical form (*vigrahānvita*).
The letter *ga*, then the letter *ya* situated upon the letter *ā* and adorned with it;
one should extract *tṛpti* mounted on Varuṇa, and *kālapāvaka*. (128)
Then there is the solitary letter *sa*, followed by the supreme consciousness (*parā saṃvit*), and then the fire (*anala*).
Then the letter *ga*, and the letter *sa* mounted upon the fire is traditionally taught [as the next]. (129)
Marked with the letter 'e' and peaceful, Varuṇa stands there;
one should then give the letter 'ra' alone, followed by the word "sarvaśakta. (130)
Endowed with the state of being the support of all, and existing both within and without all,
one should place two syllables as if they were stationary, and then [bestow] the pair of all syllables.
Having taken the supreme *prakṛti* and the letter *repha*, one should place them below that;
one should mark it with the desired [number] and then extract the letter *yakāra*.
One should then extract the letter *da* joined with the vowel *ā*, and place the letter *ga* beneath it; thereafter, O Sage, one should add the letter *ā*. (133)
O Nārada, one should then give the word "naram" marked with the letter *i*;
thereafter, the letter *ma* in two parts, and then the word "pūraya. (134)
Having taken all the syllables, the letter *ṅa* should follow immediately after;
one should place the supreme [syllable] below that, and then Nārāyaṇa in two parts.
O twice-born one, one should first mark it with the letter *ā*, then with the letter *i*;
thereafter, the letter *m* is twofold, and one should manifest the word in two ways.
The word "all" (sarvāṇi) is the instrument; then the word "time" (kālam) in two parts;
then the word "attainment of one's own self" (svātmalābhe); and then the word "apply" (niyojaya) in two parts. (137)
The Blessed One [spoke] "tryakṣaram" (the three-syllabled) and "bhavaheti" (the weapon of Bhava);
then, having taken up the Soul of Beings (Bhūtātman), he [placed] Gadādhara beneath that.
Then one should join the letter *ra*, marked with the *gopana* (the nasal bindu), upon the head; and that which stands above the *vairāja* should be marked with the syllable *oṃ*. 139.

O Brahmin, having taken the letter *ha* joined with the Lord of Space (*vyomeśa*), and the conch (*śaṅkha*) adorned with bliss (*ānanda*), one should place the Lord (*īśvara*) below that, which is flickering. 140.
One should mark it with Ānanda, and then, once [the breath] is conquered, one should apply the hand-position (pāṇipada);
having joined the four syllables, one should then place the letter Ma.
Thereafter, one should extract the Truth (the letter *Sa*) conjoined with the form of Vyomeśa (*Ha*);
then, having placed the letter *Ga*, which bestows fearlessness, immediately after that.
Vaikuṇṭha is non-different from Vyomeśa; Vārāha is adorned with the sky;
Śārṅgabhṛt is mounted upon Varuṇa; and Nyasya is marked by the sign of Vyomeśa.
The syllable *saṃ*, then the syllable *ya*—I am smeared by this three-syllabled word.
Then the syllable *sa*, the syllable *ma*, and immediately after that, the syllable *ya*. (144)
Then, taking the Lord of the Earth adorned with the syllable *oṃ*, these alone—namely the letter *pa* and the letter *va*—constitute the defining characteristics. 145.
Having taken up the Viśvabhāvaka, seated upon a lotus,
adorned with the color known as Avigraha upon his head.
Then he should utter the syllable "na," followed by the word "kevalam," and then the word "nirmalam.
O twice-born one, he should then give the word "māpādaya" and the word "sakalam."
The letter *ga* standing with the *uddāma* [vowel], then the letter *la* alone;
the Path joined with the Primordial God (*ādideva*), and Mādhava joined with Rāma. (148)
The letter *pa*, the letter *ta*, and the letter *ya* joined with the vowel *i*;
one should utter these as two separate words and give them a time marked by a triangle. (149)
Then, O twice-born one, one should join the Vairāja [syllable] mounted upon the four states; thereafter, one should place the letter *ra*, which is pervaded by that which is called Bliss.
Furthermore, O twice-born one, the state known as Someśa, situated above Vairāja, bestows this mental state; it is the five-syllabled [mantra]. 151.
Then one should assign the three-syllable mantra to verbal misdeeds; thereafter, the six-syllable mantra to physical misdeeds; and subsequently, the three-syllable mantra to those of evil conduct.
O Sage, one should then utter the five-syllabled mantra containing the word *parameśvara*; thereafter, for the supreme form, one should likewise utter the word *prasīda*. (153)
And for me, who have sought refuge, O Sage, he shall impart the five-syllabled mantra;
adorned with the letter *i*, it is the destroyer of deceit by his command. (154)
O Sage, one should place the figure of Rāma upon a man and Mādhava beneath him; and one should bestow the five-syllabled mantra, "Bhindhi saṃsāram" (Destroy the cycle of worldly existence).
Having taken the letter *da*, ascended by the worlds (*bhuvana*), conjoined with the *visarga*, which is the creator of the universe, and that alone situated at its end. (156)
O tiger among the twice-born, immediately thereafter one should extract the eternal [mantra];
then one should extract Vāmana, who is conjoined with Vyomeśa and Ananta. 157.
The path is mounted by Mādhava and adorned by Vyomeśa and Ananta;
both the letter *ka* and the letter *ra* are above the worlds. (158)
The syllable *kāla* marked with the letter *e*, adorned with *vairāja* and *rāma*;
then follows the seven-syllabled *pada* which bestows grace upon all. (159)
One should grant the station of the Self of Knowledge, conjoined with Puruṣottama;
for one who has entered into the great darkness, this indeed is the eight-syllabled station.
Having taken up that which is adorned by the source of the world, the three-syllable word for the gift is indeed the sound of the light of higher knowledge (vijñāna). || 161 ||
One should extract the letter *ha* and the letter *ma* from the entire body; then, in sequence, the three [syllables] should be joined with *nāra*, *moddāma*, and *vikramī*. 162.
The letter *bha* and the letter *va* are pervasive; these alone are you.
Mounted upon the letter *ra*, you are adorned with a garland by Padmanābha and decorated by Rāma.
The letter *ha*, the letter *ta*, and the solitary *puṇḍarīka*;
then the *vairāja* situated [therein], the lotus, and the conch marked with a triangle. || 164 ||
Then the Supreme Self, abiding in the subtle, and the solitary Puṇḍarīka;
then Rāma, situated in the letter *ta*, and thereafter the one abiding in the subtle, the Immortal. || 165 ||
Then follows the word *samuddhara*, with the letter *kā* inseparable from the vowel *e*;
then the three-syllable word *ajita*, which, O twice-born one, is the word for my birth. (166)
And from that, there is a single, short letter *na* situated in the *trāsana* (terrifying) position;
endowed with the power of sovereignty over the three worlds, it forms the word "ghātaya" twice. (167)
He should grant this sovereignty of knowledge, while the one whose feet are attached to divine play [grants] the subsequent state;
and Padmanābha, mounted upon Garuḍa, likewise goes to the abode of Kamala.
But Kamala, endowed with his beloved, resides in the Vairāja world which goes above the universe;
while Padmanābha alone is the archer adorned by Anaṅga. || 169 ||
The letter *ha*, the letter *na*, and the letter *va* adorned by *rā*;
then the Sun situated in *āhlāda*, conjoined with *madana*. (170)

One should extract the Supreme Self, endowed with the sovereignty of the three worlds, wearing a garland, mounted upon Varuṇa, and possessed of the bestowal of the sovereignty of the three worlds. (171)
The word *mama trātā* (my protector) is to be joined; then the word *sakala* (all);
then the letter *ja* and the letter *na*; then the word *śaraṇa* (refuge). || 172 ||
O Brahmin, one who has come for refuge should give the imperishable six-syllabled mantra; then the Vairāja mantra accompanied by three triangles, followed by the word of repetition, "kuruvīpsā. (173)
One should place the letter *da* alone, marked with the secret seal (*gopanāṅkita*),
and one should apply the letter *na* twice, the final one indeed marked with the secret seal.
Deya and Bhuvanapāla are accompanied by the letter *sa*, situated upon a conch;
Pantha is joined with Gopana, while Kevala obstructs all. (175)
Having uttered the supreme three-syllabled word "Puṇḍarīkākṣa," and then the word "Kāruṇika" (the Compassionate One), he was [honored] by the devotees. 176.
Having taken the word *vatsala* joined with the meditative realization of the *piṇḍa*, [he uttered] the word *viśvātmā*, and then the word *viśveśvara*. (177)
One should place the word *hṛṣīkeśa*, then the word *mokṣalakṣmī*;
then *padmanābha* with the letter *ra* situated therein, followed by the letter *da* alone. (178)
O Blessed One, the auspicious eight-syllable word is the essence of all mantras;
it is then permeated by the three triangles of the human [form], and thus becomes the state of all mantras. (179)
The syllable *puṇḍarīka* alone, marked by the letter *repha* (the letter *r*) by Viṣṇu, and further joined with *vikramī*, bestows sovereignty over the three worlds. (180)

O tiger among the twice-born, one should then place the fivefold [mantra] accompanied by the word "namo namaḥ," and subsequently the triad known as Kūṭa, Sūrya, and Amṛta, in their proper order. (181)
One should first mark with Visarga, then the word with Vyomeśa;
the third with the one named Aurva, and the fourth with Chādana.
O Nārada, the fifth [mantra] should be joined with the Yogadhātrī, and the sixth with the sixth;
one should employ Devadatta in the seventh, which is without form.
O Brahmin, Tāraka is in the eighth, Viṣṭara thereafter in the ninth;
in the tenth is Ṛtadhāmāna, and Ūrja is the eleventh, O Sage. (184)
Know that there is prosperity in the twelfth; one should place Viṣṇu in the thirteenth.
O Brahmin, one should then place Rāma in the fourteenth immediately thereafter.
Ānanda is in the fifteenth seed-syllable; after that, O Nārada, is the Praṇava with "namas" at the end, and again the Praṇava at the very end.
Again, having taken up the syllable *praṇava* and the word "Bhagavat," as well as the two-syllabled word "mama" and the word "viveka. (187)
One should give only the syllable *pa*, marked with the syllable *da* for concealment;
at the end, however, O Sage, it is marked with the *tāla* seal and devoid of the syllable *aprameya*.
By means of the goad of knowledge, one should indeed suppress the sound that arises at the appointed time as a fault;
thereafter, one should bestow the seven-syllable word, which is the lotus alone.
Then one should place Daṇḍadhāra mounted upon Viśvarūpa;
at its end, one should offer a lotus and then raise up Daṇḍadhāra.
O twice-born one, Vṛṣakarmā is below that; then Akarāla;
below him is Akhaṇḍavikramī, and Pratardana is situated beneath him.
Then, O Brahmin, the word *śaśvat* [should be placed], followed by *candrāṃśu*, and then *chandapṛṣṭhataḥ*;
it should be marked with *ānanda* which is itself marked by *vyomeśa*. (192)
Then, below that, fashion a square marked with the letter *rā*;
thereafter, one should provide a human figure marked with the letter *na*, which is itself marked by a triangle representing the three times (*kālatraya*). || 193 ||
One should employ Anala and Varuṇa alone in due order;
Puṇḍarīka is the form of Agni, and Vaikuṇṭha is the third.
One should join the three-cornered *chanda* marked [with the vowel] and then extract the moon-ray (*candrāṃśu*); then,
one should mark it with bliss (*ānanda*), mounted upon the Lord of *Chandas*.
One should utter the letter *ga* alone, followed by Vaikuṇṭha conjoined with Vyomarāja;
one should say "pūjaya" (worship) with repetition, and thereafter extract the word for the Sun (*sūrya*). (196)
At the end of *sāmadāma* (or *sāmadāma*), one should join the radiant [syllable] immediately thereafter;
at the end of the four, one should join them in sequence with eyes wide open.
O Nārada, one should place [the syllable] that bestows sovereignty over the three worlds upon the head, then the support of wisdom upon the seat;
thereafter, O Nārada, one should take up the fish mounted upon a flame.
Then, one should extract Dharmāṃśu conjoined with Vyomeśa;
finally, the essence of the Liṅga should be joined to its seat.
He is immeasurable, free from attachment, adorned with garlands, worthy of being established, and bears a plow;
the venerable Vairāja is his eastern seat.
Having extracted the fire-mantra in two ways and then assigned it to those two in sequence,
one should place Lāṅgalin and Viśvarūpa as pervasive [deities] on the exterior of the head.
One should apply the expansion of the letter by name upon the seat of the first;
immediately thereafter, one should apply that of the second, which has a long snout.
Then, having taken fire from the twice-born and placed beneath it a Sāman-leaf,
he established it upon the head of that [image] which was rooted as the support of all the worlds.
O Sage, one should place the single ether-element, enveloped by sovereignty, in two parts;
then, having taken up fire, one should place the sun below it.
Below this is fire and above it is space, situated upon Airāvata;
then, O Sage, taking the letter *ra*, it is placed upon the fish.
Above that is the radiant one, and below that is indeed fire;
the Lord of the World is situated above that, and the syllable "AṂ" is upon his head.
At the end, there are two *paṭ* syllables, followed by the solitary *lāṅgalī*;
then comes the bearer of the staff (*daṇḍadhara*) marked by Rāma, garlanded, and likewise marked by that very same [syllable]. || 207 ||
Then the word "mahāmantra," then the word "śabdena," then indeed the word "vighno 'yam," and after that the word "samaya. || 208 ||
O twice-born one, quickly act, act! [Act so that] the multitude of teeth, which removes defects, does not fail; for then the accumulation of ignorance will surely become paralyzed. 209.
Then, O Sage, having taken the Praṇava, the Sun should be joined;
thereafter, O Nārada, the Suparṇa mantra, and after that, the Prāṇa mantra. (210)
But at the conclusion of that peak, situated in the Lord of All Worlds and adorned by Vyomeśa, is my station, O Blessed One. (211)
Once it is complete, one should then provide the word joined with the description of the gift;
then the word "karmaṇi," and finally, one should form the word in two parts.
At the end of that, the word *kaustubha*, then the word *bhagavan*, and then indeed the word *amṛtamūrte* followed by *samasta*. (213)
Then follows the word-group of mantras, and after that the letter *ya* alone;
then Nārāyaṇa, who abides in the Pradhāna, and then the letter *śa* alone which bestows peace. || 214 ||
Then Nara, then Bhuvanārūḍha, then Rārūḍha, then Gadādhara;
then he whose life-breath is marked by the pervading body (Otadeha), then Śaṅkhastha, and finally Śāntida. || 215 ||
Vairāja is joined with Vyomeśa; thereafter is Sragdhara alone.
Then follows Tālalakṣmā, and at its end one should place Tṛpti below it.
Below that is Varāha; this [next] lump is marked with the Gopa;
then Nārāyaṇa alone, and again he who goes above Damanaka.
Then Mount Mandara was stepped upon by the Primordial God (Ādideva) and stood fixed like a goad;
it was joined with the vowel *au*, adorned with garlands, possessed of three corners, and radiant. || 218 ||
Then the path is exclusively [the one leading to] the state of complete satisfaction, which is twofold;
O Nārada, Soma is mounted upon Varuṇa, and that which is to be given is likewise twofold.
Then, indeed, Vyāpin, Cāndrī, and Ānanda are to be joined to the two [subsequent ones];
then Varāha, who stands in Amṛta, and beneath that, Puruṣeśvara.
For [the syllable] Uddāma is below that, Vyāpin is below that, and Cāndrī is at the head;
one should give this very same sequence again, excluding the number of worlds (bhuvanārṇa).
But the nectar [vessel] adorned by Viṣṇu should be placed there with joy;
below that, one should place the conch which is the receptacle of the nectar, and below that as well.
Then, one should perform the twofold placement of Soma, which provides nourishment for all, is endowed with bliss and the sovereignty of the three worlds, and is united with the Supreme Lord.
O Sage, Varuṇa should be given as accompanied by Bhūdharā, while Agni is to be given alone; thereafter, Daṇḍadhāra is to be given, marked with the syllable Om.
"O twice-born one, this mantra, worshipped by the thirty gods, consists of six hundred and twelve syllables: *namo namaḥ tataḥ svāhā*. (225)
"O Sage, these five half-syllables have indeed been described;
this great mantra was previously indicated and must be guarded with great effort. (226)
Even for mantras that are broken or split, yet possess a beautiful form,
this most excellent and supreme mantra shall fulfill all of them.
By his splendor, by his heroism, and always by his gentleness,
he is the great one who pacifies all defects and destroys all obstacles.
O tiger among sages, this mantra must be guarded with great effort;
it is common to all practitioners who follow the true teaching. (229)
Possessing many mouths and eyes, endowed with many feet and hands, the bestower of many wonders, and adorned with many ornaments. || 230 ||
Abounding with many fragrant flowers, bearing many weapons, possessing many blazing eyes, and adorned with many fruits. || 231 ||
He who, with a single-minded focus, constantly recollects and worships it through many tens of millions of mantras during either occasional or regular sacrifices, [attains success]. (232)
"He shall attain the perfections (siddhis) before long and shall never falter.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Ritual of the Pavitraka," in the glorious *Pāñcarātra Jayākhyasaṃhitā*.
Now begins the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Characteristics of the Conduct of Vaiṣṇavas.
Nārada:
[A question regarding the true nature of the Vaiṣṇavas, beginning with ascetics.]
O Blessed One, I desire to hear the characteristics of the Vaiṣṇavas, and especially the conduct of all those beginning with the ascetics (yatis). || 1 ||
How indeed can I know those for whom you have described the two kinds of fruit— giving and bestowing— without their defining characteristics?
The Blessed Lord: [Regarding the cause of difference despite the equality of those solely devoted to the Bhāgavata dharma:
For those who are governed by the dharma of the Blessed One and who observe the five-fold daily regimen (pañcakāla),...
And [the state] of those who do not accept gifts and subsist on gleanings of grain. || 3 ||
Those who were born into this great lineage— equal toward the external and internal, devoted to faith and self-restraint, and solely dedicated to Nārāyaṇa.
O best of Brahmins, due to the performance of rituals that are either deficient or excessive,
and also because of the power of the decline of the age, they fall into a state of imbalance.
[The characteristics of ascetics:
They have been consecrated by their father or by a preceptor through rites such as the *niṣeka*;
they abide in a state of discernment themselves and are endowed with the qualities of a celibate student (*brahmacārin*).
They perceive Viṣṇu abiding in all beings with a stainless intellect,
and they constantly contemplate that all beings abide within Him.
O high-minded one, they worship the one Adhokṣaja through action, mind, and speech; [they do so] from the dwellings of the foremost of the twice-born at the beginning, and in his absence, elsewhere.
Constantly subsisting on food obtained without asking from Brahmins devoted to the six duties,
they kept their hair, beards, and heads shaven.
Those who wear saffron-colored garments, who possess nothing more than a staff, those pure brahmins who are ascetics established in goodness (sattva), are remembered as Vaiṣṇavas. || 10 ||

[The characteristic of exclusive devotion: Having wandered for alms among those devoted to the six duties and having received them with honor, he who is indeed free from possessions should worship the Lord with that [alms-food]. (11)
The man, whose intellect is intent on discernment, dwells alone with the Great One—the unmanifest protector—with a disciple who possesses the qualities, according to the eightfold rule. 12.
By virtue of his family lineage, he is an authorized, solitary Vaiṣṇava here;
[the definition of a Vaikhānasa:
that Brahmin who, though possessing worldly attachments, worships the Supreme Lord. (13)
Whether by wealth obtained through begging from the best of Brahmins or even without being asked for,
or from a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya, he should maintain even his family.
Know that he too is a Vaikhānasa, with matted hair, carrying an umbrella, and dressed in white garments.
[The characteristic of the Karmasāttvata is: he who, for the sake of ritual action, is primarily intent upon the maintenance of his family. (15)
And even for the sake of maintaining himself, that brahmin Karmasāttvata approached the king, being intent on seeking a livelihood. (16)
[The characteristics of Śikhin:
He in whose heart the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice flashes incessantly, and for whose sake the ancestral rites and so forth are primarily performed, preceded by agriculture; || 17 ||
Indeed, Śikhin performs his duty as a preeminent brahmin in my very presence;
for although he has attained excellence, it is solely through the power of his regard for me. (18)
Nevertheless, the system of the four stages of life (cāturāśramya) is always ordained for all;
[specifically, there is a distinction of fruit for those Vaiṣṇavas such as the Vaikhānasas and others who provide a livelihood consisting of the remnants of the worship of the Blessed One].
But he who offers [a gift] for the sake of worshipping the Blessed One in a sanctuary, || 19 ||
Having established a monastery with its proper site, provided with a livelihood free from obstacles, endowed with female and male servants, and accompanied by pure and excellent Vedic scholars; (20)
They go to the abode of the Blessed One, the great dwelling place of devotees;
[this is the fruit of giving villages and so forth to Vaiṣṇava householders], or for the purpose of worshipping the Blessed One with a mind characterized by sattva. || 21 ||
And he should offer to the Vaiṣṇavas who delight in the householder’s stage of life a great amount of village land and wealth, divided among monasteries and temples.
He shall attain liberation through that which is obtained by means of the prescribed methods of righteous conduct.
[The prohibition against accepting a livelihood from anyone other than a Brāhmaṇa:
"And due to the non-attainment of alms, as well as because of his own incapacity," (23)
For the sake of not neglecting his own duties and for the maintenance of his sons and others, a Vaiṣṇava twice-born householder may do so even when extreme distress has arisen. (24)
One should receive a livelihood dependent on a temple or monastery from a Brāhmaṇa alone—
whether it be exclusively [from that source] or preceded by [income from] a village— and likewise whether obtained through begging or unasked.
By means of the ritual dedicated to Viṣṇu performed from the end of night until dawn,
that very sin indeed goes away for the sake of that purpose.
O tiger among sages, these characteristics of the Yatis and the Vaiṣṇavas have been described; now hear [those] of the Āptas and others.

[The Definition of an Authority] Those who worship the God in due order through the ritual of the five times (pañcakālya) also grant the right of eligibility to the four twice-born castes. (28) p. 250)
But when the path of the Blessed One is pure, O best of the twice-born, those Sāttvatas who abide in that essence remain unmixed with Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, and the others. (29)
By means of sacrifices to the specific deities— which are secondary and not entirely pure—
one may worship the fourfold self (Cāturātmya) consisting of Vāsudeva and the others, beginning with Saṅkarṣaṇa, excluding Vāsudeva himself.

Through the yoga of renunciation of action (*karmasaṃnyāsa*), indeed without the attainment of fruits, those who know the specific meaning of the Vedānta injunctions stand above the four [stages]. || 31 ||
O best of Brahmins, they remain with palms joined in reverence even for the sake of liberation;
yet that which appears most preeminent to them is the establishment of Hari.
Those who, having diligently acquired wealth, perform installations [of deities] and chant [the names of the Lord] with a mind endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu; || 33 ||

Brahmins who possess devotion to the Blessed One are declared to be authoritative (āpta). [The definition of an authority: Indeed, those who do not abandon the duties of their caste and perform actions as enjoined by the authorities are [authoritative]. (34)
Those who worship the deity with faith but do not attain Him are proclaimed as "anāptas" (unattainers).
[The characteristic of the Ārambhi:
Those who, for the sake of accomplishing their worldly goals, worship the Soul of the Universe without that [faith] are known as Ārambhis. (35)
Those Brāhmaṇas and others who are initiated into the Vaiṣṇava path should be known as such;
they are characterized by being those who, out of faith, engage themselves in the worship of Hari. (36)
But know, O best of Brahmins, that those who proceed by a wrong path are always to be recognized by these signs, O sage, as being among the untrustworthy (anāpta) and the like.
Now, therefore, listen briefly to the characteristics of the Vaiṣṇava practitioners who preceded [the current lineage], beginning with the Brahmins and ending with the Maudgalas. || 38 ||
[The Characteristics of Yogins:

Whether lying down, sitting, or on the path, the yogi should constantly remember the Lord dwelling in his heart; or else, according to the various distinctions such as the "partless" (niṣkala) and so forth, he should do so in a temple of Hari. 39.
Seated with eyes closed, one should constantly practice meditative absorption (samādhi);
one should utter either "Namo Nārāyaṇāya" or "Vāsudeva. (40)
One should not think of anything undesirable toward anyone through action, mind, or speech;
by these signs, those who practice the yoga of the Blessed One are to be recognized. (41)
[The characteristics of those devoted to Japan]:
He who is indeed pure, tranquil-minded, a staff-bearer, and clad in saffron robes, gazes with longing at living beings destined for the state of the Blessed One. 42.
Holding in his hand a rosary made of putrajīva, lotus seeds, or pure crystal,
he should recite the name of Hari while counting with it.
O tiger among sages, remaining intent on the worship of Viṣṇu,
one should either mutter the mantra in a low voice or recite a hymn of praise with devotion.

Know that he who is devoted to Japan is established in the Vaiṣṇava teaching; whatever vow he may undertake, let each of those be centered upon the Blessed Lord. (45) [This is the characteristic of the ascetic.]
One should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa, Parāka, and other penances, as well as the Ekādaśī and other observances, always in a temple of Viṣṇu; in the absence of such a place, while staying at home.
Whether standing or sitting, he should likewise remember Viṣṇu;
observing the month-long fast, subsisting on alms, and longing for the temple of Viṣṇu.
At the conclusion of the vow, one should worship those who are identical with the Blessed One with leaves, flowers, and other offerings;
one should perform the purification pertaining to water by immersing oneself once, twice, or thrice.
He constantly and with great effort urges those nearby to wash their two garments or to exchange them for others. (49)
He who, with a restrained soul, constantly and diligently performs such acts as this worship on the Ekādaśī day, including fasting at night—[he attains the supreme goal]. (50)
The Vaiṣṇava ascetic is said to subsist on water, roots, and fruits. [The characteristics of one who knows the scriptures:
He studies the Purāṇas, the Dharmaśāstras, and the Vaiṣṇava Itihāsas. (51)

He understands the established doctrines of Vedānta; he listens to them and even explains them, having conducted an investigation into the true meaning of those passages where the readings have been lost. (52)
Know that he who, being ever untiring, diligently refines the Āgama together with those who know it, is indeed a Vaiṣṇava who understands the scriptures. (53)

[The Characteristics of a Holder of the Treatise: He who, having collected the scripture with faith from wherever it may be found, subsequently meditates upon Brahman and then preserves it with effort; (54)
He worships the seat of the scripture (śāstrāpīṭha) in due order with offerings of water, flowers, and so forth;
he bestows it upon the Vaiṣṇavas and conceals it from those of unrefined soul.
Know him to be a bearer of the scriptures who has abandoned the views of other systems;
O Brahmin, thus has the characteristic of Vaiṣṇavas been described.
[The injunction regarding the eligibility of Vaiṣṇavas, characterized by the aforementioned definitions, for sacrifice and worship:

O Nārada, perform sacrifices and worship these [Vaiṣṇavas] with devotion and a sincere heart; for whatever śrāddha one performs in honor of a Vaiṣṇava, that indeed becomes the cause [for their liberation]. 57.

O twice-born one, this applies even to a Brahmin who has not attained [perfection], such as one among the five classes beginning with the ascetic (yati)—whether he be one who merely joins his palms in reverence, one who initiates [a rite], or one who is actively engaged in it. || 58 ||
That [offering] becomes inexhaustible for the ancestors, especially when consecrated with mantras;
and these six, O best of Brahmins, are always worthy of the ancestral rites. (59)
These six, beginning with recitation (japa), fire-oblation (homa), and vows (vrata), are likewise [performed] by the Āryas;
however, for the act of giving and in divine matters, the Kṣatriyas and others are generally prescribed.
O best of the twice-born, whatever kind of ascetics or reciters there may be, a yogi always deserves to be honored at rites for the gods and the ancestors. (61)
Even if one's age is complete, if he is devoted to yoga,
his body becomes composed of Brahman— especially so in the case of a Vaiṣṇava.
Therefore, he should indeed always be honored according to one's ability;
for future men on earth who will perform sacrifices to the Blessed One are difficult to find.
"From seeing him and from conversing with him, the eternal state is easily attained.
Nārada said:
"O Lord, indeed only one Time is heard of in the world, and no other. (64)
"Five times have been taught by you; what is this? Herein I have a doubt. The Blessed Lord:
[The distinction of the five times and the distinction of the rites to be performed therein.]
For it is of this very same single day, O Nārada, [that this was said]. (65)
From dawn until the end of night, indeed, there is a fivefold division;
this should be performed according to distinct ritual requirements, for many [fixed] times do not exist.
Nārada said:
Tell me the characteristics of actions that exist at the same time,
by the thorough knowledge of which I may become one who has accomplished his purpose.
The Blessed Lord said:

O Brahmin, beginning from the *brāhma-muhūrta* during the morning portion of the day, one should engage in recitation (*japa*), meditation (*dhyāna*), worship (*arcana*), and hymns of praise (*stotra*), accompanied by action, speech, and mind. (68)
One should approach the source of the world, and that is known as "approaching" (abhigamana).
Thereafter, having risen, one should perform the acquisition of flowers, fruits, and so forth. (69)
The supreme hour is the cause for the accomplishment of the sacrifice to the Blessed One;
it is indeed designated as its material basis, resting upon the words "karma" and "kāla."
Then, O Brahmin, one should worship the Supreme Lord with an eight-limbed sacrifice; that period of one and a half watches (six hours) is traditionally known as the time for sacrifice.
O best of sages, know that the portion of time consisting of hearing, reflection, exposition, and the recitation [of the text] together is designated as an "adhyāya. (72)
When the end of the day has arrived, having performed worship, one should practice yoga;
and at the end of the night as well, provided it is interspersed with periods of rest.
This fifth part of time, known as Yoga, bestows the perfection of Brahman.
Nārada said:
"Previously, I heard in its entirety the supreme sacrifice to the Blessed One. (74)
"I wish to hear again the details of its constituent parts in their proper divisions.
The Blessed Lord said: "From the sacrifice of the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa-yāga) up to the self-offering (ātma-nivedana)."

O Sage, that first limb of the sacrifice is the great mental identification by name, as well as the entire worship with offerings such as water for the hands (arghya), flowers, and other enjoyments. (76)
Know that, O Nārada, the worship performed with external offerings such as curds mixed with honey and clarified butter, or even with an animal sacrifice, is designated as "enjoyment" (bhoga).
O Sage, that third limb of the sacrifice is the worship with the *turyamantra*, and the offering of what has been consecrated according to the previously mentioned rule.
The fifth is traditionally known as the *saṃpradāna*, which is an auxiliary of the sacrifice;
the sixth is the satiation of the fire, and the seventh is the sacrifice to the ancestors (*pitṛyāga*). || 79 ||
The eighth is the secondary sacrifice (anuyāga) known by the name Prāṇāgnihotra.
Thus has that which was requested by you been correctly explained. (80)
"Indeed, it bestows without delay that supreme state which belongs to those established in it.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Characteristics of Vaiṣṇava Conduct," in the glorious *Jayākhyasaṃhitā* of the *Pāñcarātra*.
Thus far has been sent: now begins the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Ritual for Śrāddha," by Nārada.
O Lord, prescribe the procedure and the requirements for the rite of Śrāddha;
how should it be performed by those initiated, devoted to the Blessed One, and intent on ritual action?
The Blessed Lord:
Even by those who have been initiated, the *śrāddha* must always be performed with effort, both through ritual action and through the mind.
O twice-born one, with all debts—both those with and without interest—paid off until the end of the body.
This much alone is the secluded dharma even for perfected beings;
though a perfected being may not practice worldly dharma before others, he should still act for the sake of gathering the world. (3)
But those who have not attained perfection constantly cause great calamity;
and from that calamity of dharma, O Nārada, there arises exhaustion.
Therefore, those who possess discerning knowledge should, with great effort and diligence, protect worldly conduct as it stands, until the fall of the body. (5)
[The Preeminence of Faith in the Dharmas] "O best of sages, among all conducts and all dharmas,
such faith as I favor is indeed unsurpassed. (6)
(255) [The determination of the time and rules for the occasion of a śrāddha:
Understand its proper time and its injunctions as follows:
the twelfth days of both the bright and dark fortnights, as well as the new moon and the full moon. (7)
Upon the appearance of Rāhu as well as during the transit of the sun,
one should diligently perform the Śrāddha ceremony there with devotion according to one's desire.
On the Aṣṭakā and Anvaṣṭakā days, especially during the fortnight of the Śrāddha rites, as well as on the new moon day and the thirteenth lunar day when the moon is in the Pitṛ constellation; || 9 ||
Likewise at the first feeding of solid food for a child, during the sacramental rites for a son, or when an elder brother has returned home after the death of their father; || 10 ||

When a pure object has been obtained from a worthy person, or at a sacred ford (tīrtha), or in a temple of Hari; or when a perfected sacred site (kṣetra) has been reached, or during the consecration (pratiṣṭhā) or the rite of purification (pavitraka).

At the consecration of ponds, wells, and tanks; at the planting of trees; at the gift of a cow and similar acts; at the release of a bull; and at the commencement and conclusion of a religious vow. || 12 ||

O Brahmin, upon the completion of hearing the scripture, and likewise at its commencement, one should perform [the rite] every year for the sake of the household members, beginning with one's parents. (13)
A consecrated person should perform the *śrāddha* even on ordinary lunar days;
having first worshipped the deity and gratified the sacrificial fire, he should then perform the *śrāddha* according to the prescribed method. (14)
Then, having invited the Vaiṣṇavas according to the previously mentioned procedure,
their feet were washed, they performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), and they were sprinkled with water consecrated by the Astra-mantra.

[In that regard—the procedure for arranging the seats for the invited Vaiṣṇavas: O Nārada, [one should seat] the Lords of Mantras facing each other, or even facing north, upon separate and well-defined seats. (16)
With the Gāyatrī mantra, one should [draw] lines of ash using a wooden pin empowered with the Astra-mantra;
then, with the Hṛdaya-mantra, those [lines] consecrated by the Astra-mantra are for the seats, positioned above.
Having placed darbha grass together with sesame seeds and water,

[the following is the procedure for the manner of installation and the demonstration of the number of Vaiṣṇavas to be installed] within the group of the Guru, the group of the Fathers, and the group of the Mothers.
Or of the guru, or of the group of gurus, O Nārada, by means of the root mantra (mūlamantra).
Having first established the Vaiṣṇava [deity] upon the seat at the very beginning, one should then [proceed] with that very same [mantra] joined to the heart and adorned with *svadhā*. (19)

At the end of the row of the father, O twice-born one, he should seat another by name; then, with his head bowed and having grasped [the other's] hand with his own, [he should perform the salutation].
Having established [the deity] upon the supreme seat by means of the name belonging to the Grandfather (Brahmā),
one should [consecrate it] with the three-syllabled mantra ending in *netra* (locative case) along with its form.
One should place another Vaiṣṇava [deity] by the name of the Great-Grandfather;
these four indeed face the front of the Mantra-pīṭha.
With the four goddess-mantras, one [performs the rite] for the mother or her family; with the Astra-mantra, for the group of ancestors; facing north, there are two [mantras]. || 23 ||
[When the father and others are living, the grandfather and others are to be appointed in their place]:

"But while the father is living, O Sage, the grandfather is to be appointed in the father's place; likewise, even while the mother is present, he is indeed to be appointed in the place of her father. (24)
The maternal grandfather should always be employed with the mantra of the mother.
[Regarding the rule of restriction when Vaiṣṇavas are unavailable:
two from each of the paternal and maternal lineages, or one from each of both. (25)

O tiger among sages, one should mentally perform the ritual placement of the bodies for those who have been chosen for the positions of the ancestors and others by means of the twelve-syllable mantra;
and for all of them, the King of Weapons (the Astra-mantra) should be placed upon the palms of the hands.
[Their mode of meditation: All are to be known as four-armed, bearing the conch, discus, and mace;
they wear crowns and the kaustubha gem, and are seated upon the throne of Vainateya. || 27 ||
O Nārada, as if rising up to uplift those who have become *pretas*,
one should then perform the rite of offering water for the feet (*pādya*) and the respectful oblation (*arghya*) to the ancestors with the heart-mantra using the water from the *arghya* vessel. (28)
O Great-minded One, one should sprinkle water on each foot in succession with the root mantra; thereafter, one should take the sesame-water with both hands.
[The procedure for taking the overflow of the *arghya* water with the *pitṛ* vessel:
Having offered it again and again and having collected it into a vessel consecrated with the *astra-mantra*, one should then cover each [portion] with the three syllables of worship, O Nārada. (30)

(257) [The meditation on the ancestors in the form of Viṣṇu in their midst]: Having established them before the Blessed One, one should mentally visualize them in their midst—those ancestors in the form of Viṣṇu, resplendent with radiant bodies. (31)
Thereafter, with the Pitṛ-mantra, one should meditate right here upon the ancestors consisting of fathers and mothers,
as established in the three times seven lineages.
Then, having requested permission and received it with a bow of the head,
one should perform the sacrifice for the sake of the ancestors for those seated at their bowls and seats.
[The Petition in the Presence of Mantreśa: O Blessed One, for the sake of the ancestral sacrifice (pitr-yāga), I worship you especially;
for the sake of bestowing grace upon them, O Acyuta, perform the sacrifice for me. 34.
Having thus informed the Lord of Mantras,
one should prepare the sacrificial pap (caru) with milk.
One should observe whatever was previously prepared in the consecrated fire.
One should sprinkle the food, along with its condiments and other accompaniments, with the Astra-mantra;
having heated it over consecrated fire and having soaked it in honey and ghee.

Thereafter, having replenished [the fire] with sesame seeds and *darbha* grass as before, one should burn away everything that has been prepared, including all food such as edibles, drinks, and so forth. (37)

One should mentally conceive everything for the satisfaction of the ancestors; with that which has been prepared—such as various kinds of food and edibles—one should perform the sacrifice to the deity.
Then, one should worship the deity with that very offering, including water for the guest (arghya), flowers, and so forth.
O Nārada, having first placed them in the mandalas as prescribed,
one should then lift them up for the sake of their satisfaction, filling them completely with fruits and other offerings.
The vessels of curd, milk, and cooked rice were then offered to him in succession,
along with water for honor (arghya), flowers, incense, ointments, collyrium, and lamps.
One should contemplate that seed-syllable as being transformed within that [fire] along with its heat;
by means of that, O best of sages, one should meditate upon it as being exceedingly satisfied. (41)
One should thus lead the potency of all food to its transformation;
[this is the mantra for satiating the ancestors:
with the *praṇava*, with nectar itself, and accompanied by Vyomeśa. (42)
Then, with one's own name ending in *svadhā*, followed by "to the Self of Nārāyaṇa," and finally "salutation"— this is the mantra for the libation to the ancestors (*pitṛ-tarpaṇa*).
[Now, the procedure for the fire-oblation:
Then, O Nārada, one should proceed to the foremost [rite] in the Nārāyaṇa-fire;
having awakened it with dry fuel and [an oblation] mixed with clarified butter. (44)
Thereupon, one should place darbha grass with its tips pointing south upon the layer;
having worshipped the fire as before, he should then [worship] the ancestors established therein.
Thereafter, one should indeed worship the Mantramūrti again with an offering (bali);
with the three-syllabled mantra, one should offer three oblations of food.
Then, starting from the center of the mantra-lord's fire, moving outward from the center of that fire,
one should offer twelve oblations in a clockwise sequence.
O Nārada, one should [perform the rite] with each individual syllable of the form-mantra,
beginning with "oṃ" and ending with "svadhā," and likewise surround it on the outside with the Astra-mantra.
[Now, the procedure for offering the rice-balls (piṇḍas) to the ancestors:
